lines.text: That was in bold. For me, that's shouting.
Then be smug at everyone sheltering in doorways. You learned that from me.
My most-read sentence all week. Also my most ignored.
Summer, as advertised.
Everyone still remembers the last time you didn't.
You'll still lose a fight with it at the first gust.
That umbrella will do more for your hair than any conditioner.
Somewhere, a school is already drafting the snow-day email.
Cue the bread-and-milk panic. Nobody's ever explained the milk.
Everyone will be nine for an hour, then ninety on the ice.
You'll call it a blizzard. It'll be a dusting.
Finally, a reason to cancel the plans you were dreading.
You stopped finding it pretty about two snowfalls ago.
Straight onto the back of a chair. You'll find {GP} next week.
Or keep {GP} on out of loyalty and quietly cook.
The first afternoon without {GP} in months. Try not to make a speech.
The second you take {GP} off, you'll act like you're at the beach.
Sounds silly right now. That's exactly how it gets you.
Later you'll be the only one with {GP}. You'll mention it. Often.
First outing for {G} since spring. Brace yourself for the pockets.
You'll text someone later to bring {GP}. Again.
Or borrow someone's later and keep it for a year.
Off and on again. It fixes most things, me included.
Two outfit changes in one day. Very pop star of you.
I'll redraw you both times. No extra charge.
You'll put {GP} back on later with the face of someone who was warned.
By midday you'll doubt me. By tonight you'll apologise.
Off, then back on by tonight. You do love an on-again, off-again thing.
Iced coffee isn't water. I checked the spelling.
Every patch of shade out there will soon have someone guarding it.
I stay cool to the touch. A seatbelt buckle can't say that.
By water I mean water. Not beer, however cold.
You'll end up loitering in the freezer aisle. Again.
You'll find shade, then complain it's the wrong shade.
lines.hint: Not every hot forecast mentions shade

lines.text: You'll drink half the water, then lug the warm half around all day.
Unlike your phone battery.
Set it and forget it, like your gym membership.
So you can stop staring into the wardrobe now.
In spring, that practically makes me a miracle worker.
Best decision you'll make all day, and I made it.
That's your outfit sorted. The rest of your life, less so.
So if today goes badly, you can't blame the weather.
Now you just need somewhere to go in it.
I'd say it in a warmer colour, but I only have grey.
Somewhere, someone in shorts didn't read this.
Someone will say 'at least it's a dry cold'. All day.
So 'I'll go out once it warms up' means you're staying in.
You'll come home and hug the radiator like it's family.
Perfect for browsing flights somewhere warm and booking nothing. Again.
Somewhere a neighbour just picked up a drill. For the rest of the evening.
The trains are another story.
And there's plenty of it. It's been dark since about four.
Your 'five minutes on the sofa' will probably cover the rest of it.
Now, dinner. You haven't thought about dinner, have you.
Your group chat will spend the rest of it picking a restaurant.
Somewhere a neighbour's washing machine is just starting its spin.
You'll see the fridge light a few more times before bed, I'm guessing.
You'll spend the rest of it saying you're going to bed.
Plenty left for 'one more episode'. And the three after that.
Three outfits in one day, and you'll still say you've got nothing to wear.
Three outfits in one day. The laundry basket will hear about this.
Socks-and-sandals weather. Someone out there has waited all year for this.
The yearly heating war has begun. I'm Switzerland, but flatter.
Somebody will post a photo of one orange leaf and call it autumn.
Great leaf-raking weather. The leaves aren't worried.
Somewhere, the year's first barbecue is being lit. Badly.
Perfect day. I had someone more deserving in mind.
You'll enjoy it right up to the first sneeze.
Everyone else is away somewhere nice. You're reading a weather screen.
Someone's scraping ice off a car with a credit card. Best use it's had all month.
Someone will say spring's just around the corner. It's a long corner.
Bundled up like that, you've never looked better. Funny, that.
By the time you've got all that on, I'll need recharging.
Today the bus smells of everyone on board. Lucky I don't have a nose.
Someone will say 'it's not the heat, it's the humidity'. It's both.
Somewhere a barbecue is going ahead under an umbrella. Out of spite.
Wet leaves on every pavement. Someone's about to do an involuntary dance.
Look at that sky. It's doing your Monday face.
A bit of snow and everything closes. I'm now the most reliable service in town.
Somewhere a snowman has more personality than you. It's mostly carrot.
Light till late again, so someone will be mowing at nine.
